title: StateDelta: State-Transition Grounded Instruction Generation from Procedural Image Sequences
venue: Planned: ACL Rolling Review, January 2027 cycle, targeting ACL 2027
summary: My undergraduate Signature Work at Duke Kunshan University explores grounded instruction generation from procedural image sequences. I am developing an assembly dataset and a retrieval-augmented vision-language framework that connect instructions to specific components, attachment locations, and supported operations.
question: How can structured visual evidence and retrieval support instruction generation across furniture designs and categories while grounding each instruction in the assembly evidence?
contributions: Developing a grounded assembly dataset that links manual diagrams to detailed instructions, component annotations, and source evidence through model-assisted labeling and comprehensive human review.
Designing a pipeline from structured visual evidence through semantic and part-based retrieval to image-conditioned instruction generation.
Preparing reusable supervision for retrieval evaluation and VLM fine-tuning, with subsequent fine-tuning and RAG integration aimed at transferring knowledge from the curated assembly corpus.
limitations: Dataset development and framework design are ongoing. VLM fine-tuning, RAG integration, and cross-design transfer are intended stages of the work.
The manuscript is in preparation for a planned January 2027 ACL Rolling Review submission.
citation: Sean Wan and Kaizhu Huang. StateDelta: State-Transition Grounded Instruction Generation from Procedural Image Sequences. Manuscript in preparation; planned submission to ACL Rolling Review, January 2027 cycle.

title: ViRel-Budget: Reliability-Constrained Visual-Token Budgeting for Green Vision-Language Inference
summary: I developed a reliability-constrained pipeline that chooses a visual-token pruning budget or a dense fallback before a single VLM call, without fine-tuning the backbone. The work evaluates energy savings alongside a calibrated unsafe-acceptance limit.
question: Can a VLM use fewer visual tokens while preserving dense-model response behavior under a calibrated reliability constraint?
contributions: Constructed safety labels measuring preservation of dense-model responses on original images and eligible visual interventions.
Trained budget-specific risk predictors using pre-inference features and calibrated a policy that selects a pruning budget or dense fallback for one VLM call.
Benchmarked on POPE, MMStar, and VisualCounterFact using group-isolated prospective evaluation, independent replication draws, and paired GPU telemetry.
First-authored the paper accepted for publication at the ACM Multimedia 2026 GreenMM workshop.
findings: The SCOPE-based controller achieved replicated energy savings of 11.87% for LLaVA-1.5-7B and 10.62% for LLaVA-1.5-13B relative to matched dense inference, while meeting the calibrated unsafe-acceptance limit.
limitations: The reported savings refer to the SCOPE-based controller, matched dense LLaVA-1.5-7B and -13B inference, and the evaluated benchmark and replication settings.
Reliability is defined through preservation of dense-model responses on original images and eligible visual interventions.
citation: Sean Wan, Shilin Ou, and Luyao Zhang. ViRel-Budget: Reliability-Constrained Visual-Token Budgeting for Green Vision-Language Inference. GreenMM workshop at ACM Multimedia 2026. Accepted for publication.

title: StableEval Arena: A Cost-Aware Agentic Benchmark for Stablecoin Price Stability Prediction
theme: Reliable evaluation of agentic AI systems
venue: KDD 2026 Workshop on Evaluation and Trustworthiness of Agentic AI
summary: I built an environment-grounded historical-replay benchmark for agentic stablecoin risk assessment. It combines leakage-safe evidence windows and hidden future horizons with structured predictions, deterministic labels, calibration, and reproducible cost and latency logging.
question: How can we evaluate agentic stablecoin risk assessment while accounting for evidence leakage, calibration, rare-event failures, and computational cost?
contributions: Built the historical-replay benchmark with leakage-safe evidence windows, hidden future horizons, structured predictions, and deterministic labeling.
Integrated calibration and reproducible cost and latency logging into the evaluation.
Benchmarked six agents against always-stable, historical-persistence, threshold-rule, and logistic-regression baselines in stress-enriched and natural-distribution settings.
First-authored the paper accepted with a selected oral presentation at the KDD 2026 Workshop on Evaluation and Trustworthiness of Agentic AI.
findings: Calibrated agents surpassed historical persistence on aggregate performance in the stress-enriched evaluation.
The evaluation revealed substantial rare-event failures that accuracy alone overlooked.
limitations: The reported aggregate improvement over historical persistence applies to the enriched evaluation; it is not stated as an improvement across every evaluation setting.
Substantial rare-event failures remained despite the aggregate performance gains.
citation: Sean Wan, Dongping Liu, and Luyao Zhang. StableEval Arena: A Cost-Aware Agentic Benchmark for Stablecoin Price Stability Prediction. KDD 2026 Workshop on Evaluation and Trustworthiness of Agentic AI. Selected oral presentation.

title: Active Learning for Molecular-Docking Algorithm Selection under Heterogeneous Runtime
venue: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for Drug Discovery: Bridging the Translation Gap
summary: As a fully funded DKU Summer Research Scholar, I built a retrospective active-learning pipeline for molecular-docking algorithm selection. The work studies how partial acquisition can produce useful selector-training data when docking runtimes differ.
question: How can partial acquisition of docking outcomes support algorithm selection while accounting for heterogeneous runtime and downstream decision quality?
contributions: Integrated cell-wise acquisition, low-rank matrix completion, and runtime models fitted only to previously observed training-pool runtimes.
Trained downstream selectors on completed performance matrices while reserving held-out docking outcomes for evaluation.
Compared runtime-aware acquisition with Mean-UCB using realized docking cost, per-engine query allocation, and held-out selector performance.
First-authored the paper accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for Drug Discovery.
findings: Partial acquisition yielded decision-useful training data for docking algorithm selection.
The evaluation identified budget-dependent trade-offs between acquisition cost and downstream quality.
Matrix-reconstruction metrics did not consistently track downstream docking performance.
limitations: The study uses retrospective active learning, with runtime models fitted only to previously observed training-pool runtimes.
Cost–quality trade-offs depend on the acquisition budget, and reconstruction quality alone does not consistently indicate selector performance.
citation: Sean Wan, Jiabao Brad Wang, and Mustafa Mısır. Active Learning for Molecular-Docking Algorithm Selection under Heterogeneous Runtime. NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for Drug Discovery: Bridging the Translation Gap. Accepted.

title: Generative-AI-Assisted Portfolio Algorithm Selection under Asset-Family Shift
theme: Generalizable algorithm selection under distribution shift
venue: Planned: AAAI 2027 Workshop on Foundation Models and Generative AI for Finance (FinFM)
summary: As a fully funded DKU–SUFE Summer Research Scholar, I developed a portfolio algorithm-selection pipeline comparing LLM-generated features, pretrained time-series embeddings, and portfolio-trained Transformer representations under distribution shift.
question: Which representations help portfolio algorithm selectors transfer across asset families and forward in time?
contributions: Evaluated executable LLM-generated features, pretrained time-series embeddings, and portfolio-trained Transformer representations with random-forest and multilayer-perceptron selectors.
Built selectors to choose among classical and learned portfolio optimizers.
Investigated representation transfer through centered kernel alignment (CKA), controlled fine-tuning, family-held-out evaluation, and forward-time evaluation.
findings: In the 2025 forward test, portfolio-trained features increased mean annualized return by 12.4 percentage points over a market-feature random-forest selector.
limitations: The 12.4-percentage-point improvement is relative to the market-feature random-forest selector in the 2025 forward test.
The manuscript is in preparation, with submission to the AAAI 2027 FinFM workshop planned.
citation: Sean Wan, Haoyuan Zheng, Henghao Jiang, Zhaoxu Lin, Siyong Luo, and Mustafa Mısır. Generative-AI-Assisted Portfolio Algorithm Selection under Asset-Family Shift. Manuscript in preparation; planned submission to the AAAI 2027 Workshop on Foundation Models and Generative AI for Finance (FinFM).
